assumptions: USD and UTC are adapter conventions; the source does not supply a timezone.
User + Card scopes history. Positive purchases only; original source values and labels are preserved.
Blank Errors? is treated as completed; other values as failed attempts.
History starts with the supplied file. No hidden warmup or merchant-fraud feedback is added.
Is Fraud? is used only to compare outcomes, never as a model input.
Card IDs are not devices. Missing graph context is explicitly unknown.

samples.description: Follow five everyday purchases and inspect each connection.
samples.guidance: With only five payments, Upload-v9 has very little history. Start here to learn the graph.
samples.selection: First 5 positive purchases for user 424 from 2018-02-01.
samples.title: First five payments

samples.description: Explore a compact card history with a labeled online fraud episode.
samples.guidance: Compare the source labels with the model alerts. A short history can leave fraud undetected.
samples.selection: Last 50 positive purchases for user 591, card 1, before 2018-12-02.
samples.title: A short online history

samples.description: Investigate a burst of labeled fraud among an established purchase history.
samples.guidance: Run Simulate, then open Events to inspect alerts and Results to compare them with the source labels.
samples.selection: Last 250 positive purchases for user 759 before 2018-11-18.
samples.title: An online fraud episode

samples.description: Explore chip, swipe and online purchases across one user's cards.
samples.guidance: A labeled fraud episode does not guarantee an alert. Compare detection across the different payment channels.
samples.selection: Last 1,000 positive purchases for user 1497 in 2018.
samples.title: Across payment channels

samples.description: Move between account groups and inspect a larger mix of ordinary and fraudulent purchases.
samples.guidance: Open transaction groups to narrow the network, then inspect individual payments and their history.
samples.selection: Last 5,000 positive purchases in 2018 across the 13 selected users.
samples.title: Many accounts, one view

samples.description: Explore 10,000 transactions at the interactive workspace's supported limit.
samples.guidance: The graph groups larger histories. Loading and simulation take longer; use groups to reach individual payments.
samples.selection: Last 10,000 positive purchases in 2018 across the 13 selected users.
samples.title: The full workspace

selectionScope: Curated demonstrations from previously inspected IBM data, not a new independent evaluation. User and time windows were chosen to illustrate known fraud episodes; no model or threshold tuning.
